physical_harm: Deceased consumed poison and died in hospital
number_of_offences: Charged with 2 offences, both finally upheld
key_evidence_accepted: The deceased consumed poison from a small bottle he carried in his pocket at his own house, and there is no material to show that the appellant abetted the suicide of the deceased.
witness_credibility: The court found the complainant's and other witnesses' statements to be self-serving and not credible, as they did not provide any material to show the appellant's relation with the deceased or her involvement in the alleged offences.

trial_duration.high_court_decision: High Court rejected application of appellant u/s.482, CrPC
trial_duration.supreme_court_decision: Allowing the appeal, the Court set aside cognizance order/NBW and proceedings u/s.306, IPC and 3(2)(v) of the SC and ST Act

investigation_status: FIR registered on 11.05.2018, charge sheet filed only against the appellant for the offence under Section 306 IPC and Section 3(2)(v) of the Act, cognizance taken against the appellant, non-bailable warrants issued on 21.02.2019, case registered in Special Sessions Trial No.23 of 2019 pending

appeal_history.trial_court: Cognizance order/NBW issued against the appellant
appeal_history.high_court: High Court rejected application of appellant u/s.482, CrPC
appeal_history.supreme_court: Appeal allowed, cognizance order/NBW and proceedings set aside

prosecution_argument: The deceased was maintaining a relation with the appellant, and as she refused to marry him, he committed suicide by consuming poison. The appellant and other family members abused the deceased by uttering casteist words, which constitutes an offence under Section 3(2)(v) of the SC and ST Act.
defence_argument: There is absolutely no basis to proceed against the appellant for the alleged offence under Section 306 IPC and Section 3(2)(v) of the SC and ST Act. Except for self-serving statements, there is no material to show that the appellant was maintaining any relation with the deceased or abetted his suicide. The High Court erred in rejecting the application under Section 482, CrPC.
legal_principle_applied: Abetment involves a mental process of instigating or intentionally aiding a person in doing an act. To convict under Section 306 IPC, there must be an active act or direct act that led the deceased to commit suicide, seeing no option, and that act must have been intended to push the deceased into such a position.
precedent_relied_upon: Chitresh Kumar Chopra v. State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi) (2009) 16 SCC 605; Amalendu Pal @ Jhantu v. State of West Bengal (2010) 1 SCC 707; S.S. Chheena v. Vijay Kumar Mahajan & Anr. (2010) 12 SCC 190; Rajiv Thapar & Ors. v. Madan Lal Kapur (2013) 3 SCC 330
other_sentence_order: The cognizance order/NBW as well as proceedings under Section 306 IPC and 3(2)(v) of the SC and ST Act against the appellant were set aside. The application filed under Section 482 CrPC was allowed.
